stories.headline: [Tuko News] Kenya to Host 4th Global Military AI Summit in Nairobi in 2027 Kenya will host the 4th global military AI summit in Nairobi in 2027, positioning the country as a key player in discussions on Artificial Intelligence and defense
stories.summary: Kenya will host the 4th Global Military AI Summit in Nairobi in 2027, marking the first time the event will be held in Africa. The summit will bring together the global community to discuss the governance of military artificial intelligence and its implications for international peace, safety, and ethics. This hosting position reinforces Nairobi's role in the initiative and establishes Kenya as a key player in discussions on AI and defense. The 2027 edition aims to shape crucial frameworks where military AI meets international standards. The event is part of a series, with previous and upcoming summits, including the AI Tomorrow Summit 2025 and 2026, held in other locations, such as Ankara. Kenya's hosting of the summit is seen as a significant development in the country's engagement with global AI and defense discussions.

stories.headline: [Malay Mail] Traveling to Japan? Visa fees go up fivefold from July TOKYO, June 20 — The Japanese government on Friday decided to raise single-entry visa fees for foreigners fivefold to 15,000 yen (US$90; RM384.83) from 3,000 yen
stories.summary: The Japanese government has decided to raise single-entry visa fees for foreigners fivefold to 15,000 yen (US$90; RM384.83) from 3,000 yen, effective July. This marks the first increase since 1978 and is attributed to inflation and the yen's depreciation. The new fee will be implemented in July, affecting all foreigners applying for single-entry visas to Japan. The significant increase is expected to impact tourism and travel to the country. The previous fee of 3,000 yen had been in place for over four decades, and the new fee of 15,000 yen will be a substantial change for visitors planning to travel to Japan. The government's decision aims to adjust to current economic conditions, with the yen's value having depreciated over time.

stories.headline: [Focus Taiwan] Drones, AI put Ukraine at center of Europe defense show Ukraine's battlefield experience has made the country a focal point of this year's Eurosatory defense exhibition in France, with military planners and defense contractors
stories.summary: Ukraine's battlefield experience has made it a focal point at the Eurosatory defense exhibition in France, with military planners and defense contractors seeking lessons in drone warfare and innovation. The country's use of drones, AI, and other technologies in its war with Russia is in the spotlight. Military planners are focusing on autonomous and remotely operated systems, including loitering munitions and anti-tank guided weapons, after observing their effectiveness in recent conflicts. Ukraine's drone campaign has disrupted Russian supply lines, but electronic warfare defenses remain intact, with radio jammers rendering the electromagnetic spectrum hostile to remote-controlled drones. Meanwhile, Russia has continued to attack Ukraine with missiles and drones, including a recent barrage on the eve of new direct talks in Istanbul. The exhibition highlights Ukraine's growing importance in European defense discussions.

stories.headline: [Inbox.eu] “Ukraine Also Didn’t Believe”: Professor Warns Baltic States of the Risk of Russian Invasion The Baltic States are generally responding correctly to threats from Russia; however, they do not speak openly enough about the possibility of direct military action
stories.summary: A professor is warning the Baltic States of the risk of a Russian invasion, stating they do not openly discuss the possibility of direct military action enough. Despite the Baltic States responding correctly to Russian threats, the professor believes they should be more vocal about the potential for invasion. This warning comes after 14 Eastern European countries joined NATO in the past week, seeking protection from the Russian threat. Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022 was reportedly driven by distorted threat perceptions within the Kremlin. Intelligence services now warn that Russian leadership may operate in isolated informational environments, increasing the risk of misinterpreting Western actions and escalating tensions. The US is advised to shift the burden of Baltic security to European NATO members while reaffirming its commitment to the alliance's Article 5 guarantees.

stories.headline: Discord begins testing age verification with Google Wallet and credit cards, but face scans are still on the table
stories.summary: Discord has begun testing age verification methods, including Google Wallet and credit cards, in addition to previously announced face scans and government-issued ID scans. The platform will require users to verify their age to access adult content as part of its "teen by default" approach. Users will have the option to choose between scanning a government-issued ID, recording a video selfie for facial age estimation, or using Google Wallet or credit cards. This change affects over 200 million monthly users and is intended to enhance children's safety on the platform. The new age verification methods are expected to roll out in the coming months, with the goal of creating a safer environment for users. The testing phase is currently underway, with users soon to be required to verify their age to access certain content.

stories.headline: Microsoft is killing Office 2021 in 2026, and it's pushing hard for 365
stories.summary: Microsoft will be ending support for Office 2021 in 2026, pushing users towards its Microsoft 365 subscription service. Office 2021 is available for both Windows and Mac, but the company is encouraging users to switch to a Microsoft 365 Personal, Family, or Premium subscription. This subscription offers AI features, although they are only available to the subscription owner and cannot be shared. Usage limits also apply. The shift away from Office 2021 is part of Microsoft's effort to transition users to its cloud-based subscription model. The KMS client key for Office 2021 is FXYTK-NJJ8C-GB6DW-3DYQT-6F7TH, with a license valid for 180 days that can be automatically renewed. As the end of support approaches, users will need to consider upgrading to Microsoft 365 to continue receiving updates and support.

stories.headline: Nothing Teases First-Ever B Series Device in India: New Smartphone Launch Tipped
stories.summary: Nothing, a UK-based tech company, has begun teasing the launch of its first-ever B series device in India. The company, known for its unique designs and transparent aesthetics, has not revealed many details about the upcoming device. However, this teaser marks the introduction of a new product line in the country. Nothing has been expanding its presence in India, with plans to manufacture its flagship smartphone, the Phone (3), locally. The company has also been rumored to be working on the Nothing Phone (4a), which is expected to feature the Snapdragon 7s Gen 4 chipset. An official launch date has not been announced, but more information is expected to be revealed soon. The launch of the B series device is anticipated to further strengthen Nothing's position in the Indian market.

stories.headline: A More Realistic Octagon: EA SPORTS UFC 6 Launches on the 20th
stories.summary: EA SPORTS UFC 6 is set to launch on June 19, 2026, for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. The game promises a more realistic experience, featuring detailed cuts, bruises, and damage, as well as a dynamic stamina system that impacts every strike. The gameplay trailer showcased impressive graphics, with some users noting that the animation is still a work in progress. Electronic Arts Inc. officially announced the game on May 5, 2026, and it is expected to be available in various regions, including Korea, where a package version for PS5 was released in collaboration with Gamepia. The game's release is highly anticipated, with fans eagerly awaiting the chance to step into the Octagon on June 19.

stories.headline: JJ Gabriel's Premier League ban lifted as Man United wonderkid set new timeline
stories.summary: JJ Gabriel's Premier League ban has been lifted, allowing him to play in the upcoming season. The Manchester United wonderkid was previously barred from competing in the Premier League due to his age. Gabriel has already made a name for himself, scoring in the FA Youth Cup match against Peterborough United and receiving the U18's Premier League award. With the ban lifted, he has the entire season to become Manchester United's youngest-ever Premier League player. He also has the opportunity to break the record for youngest Premier League goal scorer, currently held by Arsenal's Max Dowman, who scored at 16 years and 73 days old. Gabriel's pathway to the first team is now clear, and he may feature in the upcoming season as the club looks to showcase its youth development.

stories.headline: Liverpool have key advantage over £100m Yan Diomande transfer that PSG can't match
stories.summary: Liverpool are in talks with RB Leipzig to sign Yan Diomande, valued at around £120m. The player is keen on the move, and Liverpool have an advantage over rival suitors PSG, who are unable to match the high transfer fee. Liverpool's second bid for Diomande is reportedly around £105 million, although RB Leipzig are holding out for approximately £112m. The Reds remain locked in negotiations, seeking to secure the transfer. Diomande's interest in joining Liverpool gives the club an edge in the pursuit, with PSG's inability to pay the high fee working in Liverpool's favor. The transfer talks are ongoing, with Liverpool aiming to finalize the deal.

stories.headline: Marcus Rashford plan, Tchouameni latest and Fernandes
stories.summary: Manchester United is making moves in the transfer market, with several players being considered. Marcus Rashford's future is a topic of discussion, with a plan in place for the striker. Aurélien Tchouameni is the latest target, with the club exploring options to sign the midfielder. Meanwhile, a deadline has been set for a deal involving Bruno Fernandes. Other players, such as Yan Diomande, Elliot Anderson, and Kenan Yıldız, are also being linked to the club. Additionally, Michael Olise and other targets are being considered as part of the club's transfer strategy. The club is working to finalize deals, with updates expected on the status of these transfers. Fans can stay informed about the latest developments through the Manchester Evening News.

stories.headline: Liverpool news: Andoni Iraola could sign Jurgen Klopp target as transfer deadline set
stories.summary: Andoni Iraola, Liverpool's new head coach, is actively pursuing new signings in his first transfer window. Victor Munoz is set to join the Reds, and Iraola may also target a player previously sought after by Jurgen Klopp. The summer transfer window is crucial for Liverpool's rebuild, and Iraola has already made changes, confirming his first squad rule alteration. The players have reportedly made their feelings clear on the new rules. Iraola may also reinstate two key rules introduced by Klopp that were scrapped by his predecessor, Arne Slot. With the transfer deadline approaching, Liverpool fans await further announcements on new arrivals and potential departures. Iraola's swift action in the transfer market indicates his intention to shape the squad according to his vision.

stories.headline: Not blood, but ideology determines the heir, says Eknath Shinde
stories.summary: Eknath Shinde, the 10th Deputy Chief Minister of Maharashtra, emphasized that ideology, not bloodline, determines the heir in Shiv Sena's legacy. He made this statement during the celebration of Shiv Sena's 60th foundation day, criticizing Uddhav Thackeray and the potential decline of the party's strength due to Congress mergers. Shinde stated that true Shiv Sainiks are those who uphold the party's ideology, not those claiming legacy through blood relations. He also took a swipe at Uddhav Thackeray, saying that political leadership is built through work and commitment, not lineage alone. This statement signals potential political shifts and underscores Shinde's commitment to the party's ideology over family ties. Shinde's comments are seen as a significant development in the ongoing political landscape of Maharashtra.

stories.headline: Police, probe agencies get app to scan fingerprints on the go
stories.summary: The National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) has launched an app called Abhigyan, allowing police and investigating agencies to scan fingerprints on the go. The app is linked to a national database of 1.3 crore criminal records, enabling officers to check an individual's criminal history within a minute. Portable fingerprint scanners are connected to the app, allowing police to take a suspect's thumb impression and verify their details instantly. This technology aims to enhance the capabilities of police and investigating agencies, providing them with a quick and efficient way to identify suspects and access their criminal records. The app is expected to aid in crime investigation and prevention, with police able to use it to scan fingerprints on the streets and in the field.

stories.headline: How the RSS changed its constitution to defend legal status and guru dakshina
stories.summary: Karnataka Home Minister Priyank Kharge's letter to RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat has led to a defense of the RSS's legal status and guru dakshina. The RSS has pointed to decades-old Income Tax rulings to justify its financial transparency. Under Indian law, not all organizations are required to register, and registration is done based on the type of function of the organization. The RSS has changed its constitution to defend its legal status. The organization has cited laws like the Societies Registration Act, which allows registration depending on the type of function. The RSS has also referenced Income Tax rulings from decades ago to support its stance on financial transparency and guru dakshina. The move comes amid demands for financial transparency from the Karnataka Home Minister.

stories.headline: Wanted her removed, but ‘no major argument’: What Delhi doctor's wife said in house help murder
stories.summary: A Delhi doctor, Manish Gupta, has been arrested for allegedly murdering his 45-year-old domestic help, Meena Haldar, in South Delhi's Mount Kailash area. The doctor claimed the victim brought "bad energy" into the home, negatively affecting his son's studies. Gupta's family reported differences with the house help, but his wife stated there was no major argument. The doctor allegedly used a bat and a knife to commit the crime. A court has granted two-day police custody of Gupta to recover evidence and examine possible involvement of others. The investigation is ongoing, with police seeking to determine the circumstances surrounding the murder and potential motives. Gupta's wife had wanted the house help removed, but the exact events leading to the murder are still being probed.

stories.headline: The Canberra Times] Mission accomplished? The sorry legacy of the brief war with Iran is enough to make you weep
stories.summary: A brief but brutal three-month war with Iran has ended with no substantial achievements, despite costing billions of dollars and up to 10,000 lives. The conflict has reshaped the Middle East and eroded public trust in politicians in the countries that launched the war. A US military intelligence assessment concluded that airstrikes on Iran's nuclear infrastructure failed to cripple the country's atomic ambitions. The war's outcome has been criticized, with some arguing that it achieved nothing of substance. The Iran deal remains in place, and Iran's stockpile of highly enriched uranium was cited as a goal, but the war's impact on this issue is unclear. The geopolitical landscape has been left more unstable, with long-term consequences for the region and global politics. The war's legacy is widely regarded as sorry and devastating.

stories.headline: [The Globe and Mail] war disgrace cripples the U.S. and elevates China
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump asked Chinese President Xi Jinping for China's help in reopening the Strait of Hormuz during the Beijing Summit. This request has been seen as a symbol of the US's weakened position, with some governments viewing China as a more stable alternative to the US under Trump's leadership. The development comes amid rising tensions between the US and Iran, which has been described as a "war disgrace" for the US. As a result, China's global influence appears to be growing, with the country being perceived as a more reliable partner. However, China's stability is maintained through tight control of information, raising concerns about its intentions. The shift in global dynamics has significant implications for international relations and the balance of power between major nations.

stories.headline: [Daily Excelsior] Climate Change and its Impact on Agricultural Sector
stories.summary: Climate change is projected to aggravate yield fluctuations of many crops, with significant impacts on the agricultural sector. Rising temperatures and changing weather patterns are expected to affect human health, food security, and economies globally. In regions like Jammu & Kashmir, unique agro-climatic conditions and difficult terrain make it vulnerable to climate-related challenges. The Minister has urged the Union to address these concerns, highlighting the need for adaptation and mitigation strategies. Studies suggest that even a 2°C increase in temperature could lead to extreme rainfall, drought, and land subsidence, further exacerbating the situation. The impact of climate change on agriculture is a pressing concern, with potential consequences for food security and economic stability. Efforts to address these challenges are crucial to ensuring the long-term sustainability of the agricultural sector.

stories.headline: No fourth headline available, only three provided
stories.summary: As of May 2025, no fourth federal stimulus check has been authorized by Congress or announced by the IRS. Despite this, misleading headlines and scam messages are circulating online, suggesting eligibility for new stimulus checks. These messages often claim recipients are eligible for $2,000 or $1,400 checks in 2025. The IRS and Congress have not made any announcements about a new stimulus check, making these claims likely scams. Individuals are advised to be cautious of texts, emails, and social media posts making such claims, as they may be attempts to deceive or steal personal information. The lack of official confirmation from the IRS or Congress indicates that these claims are false, and people should rely on trusted news sources for accurate information on stimulus checks and other government announcements.

stories.headline: Aequs, Nykaa Lead Weekly Gains Among New-Age Tech Stocks
stories.summary: Aequs and Nykaa led the weekly gains among new-age tech stocks, with Aequs emerging as the biggest gainer. Its shares surged 21.42% to end at ₹221.9, driven by positive investor sentiment. This comes after a week of stock-specific movement in the new-age tech sector, marked by volatility. Other gainers included Shadowfax, Ather Energy, and Honasa Consumer. In recent weeks, various new-age tech stocks have seen significant gains, such as EaseMyTrip, which rose 23.7% last week, and ideaForge, which gained 18.4% ahead of its Q4 results. The gains are part of a broader trend of momentum stocks experiencing movement amid market volatility, with 31 out of 57 new-age tech stocks under Inc42's tracker showing stock-specific movement.

stories.headline: Ola Electric, Ather Slip As 14 New-Age Tech Stocks Post Weekly Losses
stories.summary: Ola Electric and Ather Energy were among 14 new-age tech stocks that posted weekly losses, despite 43 of 57 stocks in the sector gaining between 0.08% and 21%. Ola Electric trimmed its Q2 net loss by 15% year-over-year and 2% quarter-over-quarter to INR 418 crore. However, its stock slipped, while Ather Energy hit an all-time high before falling 4.29%. BlueStone was the biggest loser, dropping 12.33% to ₹428.35. The losses come as Ola Electric has been experiencing a decline in market share, while Ather Energy reported a 50% year-over-year rise in operating revenue. Ola Electric's revenue slipped, but its losses narrowed to INR 418 crore in the quarter. The stock movements reflect the volatility in the new-age tech sector, with some companies showing promise while others struggle to find their footing.

stories.headline: 43 New-Age Tech Stocks Gain Up To 21% In Weekly Trade
stories.summary: 43 out of 57 new-age tech stocks gained between 0.08% and 21% in weekly trade, while 14 stocks fell by 0.21% to nearly 8%. The top tech stock movers included KLA, with a 24.59% rise, Applied Materials with an 18.25% gain, and Sandisk with a 17.94% increase. The gains come after a modest weekly performance, following a sell-off induced by the FOMC meeting. Lower oil prices and yield stabilization have encouraged dip buying, contributing to the uptrend. The new-age tech stocks saw stock-specific movement amid ongoing market volatility, with some stocks experiencing significant gains and others experiencing losses. The tech industry continues to experience real-time updates and headlines, with investors staying informed about the latest developments.

stories.headline: New-Age Tech Stocks Post Mixed Results With 14 Stocks Falling Up To 8%
stories.summary: New-age tech stocks posted mixed results, with 24 out of 41 stocks gaining between 0.06% and 9%, while 17 stocks declined between 0.67% and over 8%. The declines were led by 14 stocks that fell up to 8%. This volatility comes amid a broader rotation from tech to value names in the US stock market. Recently, megacap tech giants such as Alphabet, Meta, and Microsoft reported quarterly results, with Alphabet's shares rising 2.5%. Other tech stocks, including Spotify and Uber, saw declines of 2% and 5% respectively in post-earnings moves. The mixed performance of new-age tech stocks reflects the ongoing uncertainty in the market, with some large technology stocks like Microsoft and NVIDIA rising, while others like Apple fell. The sector's performance is being closely watched amid the shifting market trends.

stories.headline: Ghana eyes local control of Gold Fields’ biggest mine in push for more gold revenue
stories.summary: Ghana is considering transferring control of the Gold Fields Tarkwa mine to local firms when its leases expire next April. This move is part of a push to increase local control of the country's gold mining industry and boost revenue. The Tarkwa mine is Gold Fields' biggest mine in the country. Ghana has already taken similar steps with the Damang Gold Mine, which was previously run by South Africa-based Gold Fields. The Damang mine has been handed over to local firm Engineers & Planners Ltd. The Ghanaian government's efforts aim to increase domestic participation in the mining sector and retain more of the revenue generated from gold mining within the country. The transfer of control is expected to take place when the current leases expire in April next year.

stories.headline: Two Vietnamese women charged in chicken feet smuggling worth US$13mil
stories.summary: Hanoi police have charged two Vietnamese women, Nguyễn Thị Tố Loan, 47, and Trang Tuyết Ngọc, 45, with smuggling after an investigation found their company imported hundreds of containers of frozen chicken feet from countries with active poultry diseases. The women allegedly sold the smuggled goods, with the total value estimated at US$13 million. The two suspects have confessed to their involvement, admitting to overseeing the import of 339 containers of frozen chicken feet. The Hanoi City Police investigation agency has opened a criminal case against them and ordered their detention. The investigation found that the chicken feet were imported from countries with active poultry diseases, posing a potential risk to public health. The women are being held in pre-trial detention pending further proceedings.

stories.headline: CREDICORP rolls out new credit scheme in Ogun
stories.summary: CREDICORP, the Nigerian Consumer Credit Corporation, has launched a new credit scheme in Ogun State. The scheme aims to help Nigerians acquire vehicles and other essential assets. This expansion is part of CREDICORP's nationwide consumer credit rollout. Interested working Nigerians can visit the company's website, www.credicorp.ng, to express interest in receiving consumer credit. The deadline for application is May 15, 2024. As a government-backed financial institution, CREDICORP's goal is to make credit accessible to Nigerians, promoting financial inclusion and economic growth. The launch in Ogun State marks a significant step in achieving this objective, providing citizens with increased access to credit facilities.

stories.headline: Dolce & Gabbana Eyes Growth in Menswear, Lifestyle & Global Expansion
stories.summary: Dolce & Gabbana is focusing on growth in menswear, lifestyle, and global expansion. Co-CEO Stefano Cantino discussed the brand's potential ahead of its men's spring 2027 show in Milan. The show featured a menswear wardrobe inspired by Sicily, with models showcasing outfits suitable for both hot city streets and beach escapes. The collection included the signature #DGCarretto print, highlighting the brand's Made in Italy heritage. As part of its expansion plans, Dolce & Gabbana aims to increase its presence in the menswear market and lifestyle sector, while also exploring new global markets. The brand's strategy is expected to be driven by its commitment to Italian craftsmanship and high-quality products. With its new collection and expansion plans, Dolce & Gabbana is poised for growth in the fashion industry. The brand's men's spring 2027 show in Milan marked a key step in this direction.

stories.headline: Nobel Prize winner John Jumper quits Google DeepMind after nearly a decade; set to join Anthropic
stories.summary: Nobel Prize winner John Jumper has left Google DeepMind after nearly nine years to join Anthropic. Jumper announced his decision on social media platform X, stating he would join Anthropic after taking time to recharge. His departure comes amid intensifying competition for top AI talent in the sector. Jumper played a central role in developing AlphaFold, an AI project, just six months after joining Google DeepMind. He led the project and made significant contributions during his tenure. Jumper's move to Anthropic marks a significant shift in his career, with the details of his new role not yet disclosed. His resignation from Google DeepMind is effective immediately, with Jumper set to join his new employer after a brief period of recharge.

stories.headline: AI Didn’t Kill Coding Jobs. It Created a New Industry
stories.summary: Contrary to predictions, artificial intelligence has not replaced software developers, but instead created a new industry. Despite over 100,000 tech jobs disappearing due to automation, the demand for skilled programmers remains high. In 2024, there were 28.7 million developers, and this number is projected to increase by 2030. The narrative that AI would replace coders has been debunked, with experts arguing that AI has augmented the work of programmers, allowing one programmer to do the work of many. This shift has led to the creation of new job opportunities in fields related to AI development and implementation, rather than replacing existing coding jobs. As a result, the tech industry continues to evolve, with AI driving innovation and growth, rather than replacing human workers. The number of developers is expected to continue growing, with new opportunities emerging in the field.

stories.headline: Amazon’s Movie Arm Abandons Film About OpenAI
stories.summary: Amazon's movie arm, Amazon MGM Studios, has abandoned the upcoming film "Artificial," a biopic about OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. The movie, directed by Luca Guadagnino and starring Andrew Garfield as Altman, was set to tell the story of Altman's journey to becoming the chief executive of OpenAI. The decision comes after Amazon and OpenAI deepened their ties earlier this year, with Amazon recently closing a $50 billion deal with the company. The film's cancellation represents a notable example of Big Tech's influence on Hollywood, with Amazon opting not to produce a movie about a key figure in the industry. The move highlights the complex relationships between tech companies and the entertainment industry.

stories.headline: Google announces major breakthrough in AI-powered chip design with new processor
stories.summary: Google has announced a major breakthrough in AI-powered chip design with a new processor, marking a significant development in its efforts to enhance AI capabilities. The company has also committed to using multiple generations of Intel chips to power its AI data centers, expanding an existing partnership. This collaboration aims to advance the next generation of AI and cloud infrastructure. Additionally, Google is rolling out its powerful Ironwood AI chip, which targets Nvidia's market share. The new AI chips are focused on inference, a critical aspect of AI processing. The partnership with Intel will see Intel Xeon processors continue to power Google Cloud infrastructure across AI, inference, and general-purpose workloads. This development underscores Google's push to improve its AI offerings and stay competitive in the rapidly evolving tech landscape.
